summary.intent: Implement 'PR C' (finding A5 from a plan) in Callisto: add a repository-metadata check to the release registry provider's preflight, querying the `repository` field for npm and Cargo, stacked on top of PR B.
summary.outcome: Added a new provider/repository.rs module and wired it into the registry provider with tests, a spec criterion, an architecture doc note and a changeset. `just ci` passed (exit=0), and the change was committed, pushed and opened as PR C stacked on PR B.

repo: Callisto release providers live under crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/, with the registry provider in registry.rs and its tests in registry/tests.rs.
Release behavior is documented in docs/specs/release.json (acceptance criteria) and docs/architecture/release.md, and both are updated alongside code changes.
User-facing changes require a changeset, and the full `just ci` run is the gate before shipping a PR.
Work is done in git worktrees (.claude/worktrees/smoke-main) and PRs are stacked (PR C on PR B).

code.finding: New module holding the repository-metadata check, with `repository` queries for npm and Cargo; declared in provider/mod.rs and called from the registry provider preflight.

workflow: Edits were applied through small helper scripts in /tmp (Python edit scripts and shell scripts for test and CI runs), which kept multi-file changes reproducible.
Run the narrow format and test pass first, then full `just ci` and check the exit code before committing and opening the PR.
Stacking PRs (C on B) keeps each change reviewable, with the PR body written to a file and passed to the PR command.

open_items: PR C is stacked on PR B, so it depends on B merging first and may need a rebase or retarget afterward.
